static_role_design.intended_use: Owns VinOps database objects and security-definer functions; not an application or worker runtime identity.
Application transaction role after set_request_context(actor, correlation).

static_boundary.application_role_grants: USAGE on vinops schema; SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on tables; DELETE revoked; RLS policies are intended to constrain visibility and writes.
static_boundary.worker_role_grants: USAGE on vinops schema and EXECUTE on claim_outbox_events, mark_outbox_published and mark_outbox_failed; no generic table grant is recorded in this migration.
static_boundary.public_function_access: ALL functions in the vinops schema are revoked from PUBLIC before explicit grants.
static_boundary.request_context: vinops.set_request_context sets actor and correlation settings transaction-locally.

candidate_policy_groups.candidate_guard: active organization/project membership and server-derived actor context
can_read_scoped_resource for reads and can_manage_project_context for writes
current actor / self-owned session data with selected security-definer lookup functions
actor, project/organization access, or fixed worker function depending on table

required_runtime_matrix.assertion: Migration creates all roles, policies and RLS protections from an empty disposable database.
Application connection assumes vinops_app and cannot run with an owner/superuser/bypass-RLS identity.
Two synthetic tenants prove permitted same-tenant reads/writes and denied or invisible cross-tenant reads/writes, including USING and WITH CHECK behavior.
A transaction without a request actor cannot use tenant tables as an application context.
Worker connection assumes vinops_worker and can operate only through its fixed outbox procedures.
